summary: Nusatupe Airport serves the town of Gizo, the capital of Western Province in the Solomon Islands, and sits on a small island just off the main town connected by a short causeway. The airport is a vital gateway to some of the Pacific's most renowned dive sites, including the WWII wrecks and barrier reef systems surrounding the New Georgia Islands. Its modest single-runway setup reflects the remote and laid-back character of the Western Province.
faqs:
Q: How do I get from Nusatupe Airport to Gizo town?
A: The airport is located on Nusatupe Island, only a short walk or quick taxi ride across the causeway to central Gizo. Most accommodations and dive operators are within a few minutes of the terminal.

Q: Are there regular flights to Nusatupe Airport?
A: Yes, Solomon Airlines operates scheduled domestic flights connecting Gizo with Honiara and other provincial centers. Schedules can be weather-dependent and flights are limited, so booking in advance is recommended.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: Nusatupe is a small regional airport with a modest terminal offering basic services. There are no jet bridges, and passengers typically walk directly onto the tarmac. Expect limited amenities, so bring any essentials with you.

Q: Can I get a rental car at Nusatupe Airport?
A: Rental cars are not typically available at the airport. Most visitors arrange transport through their hotel or use local taxis, which are inexpensive and readily available.
transport_tips: Taxis and hotel transfers are the most common way to reach Gizo town from the airport, as the terminal is just minutes away. Local buses and shared trucks serve the area but are infrequent. If arriving on a later flight, pre-arrange a transfer with your hotel, as transport options thin out in the evening.
local_tip: Pack reef-safe sunscreen and quick-dry gear in your carry-on—Gizo's dive operators can sometimes pick you up directly from the airport for early-morning trips to nearby WWII wrecks and reefs like Munda and the Kennedy Islands.
